### An Ordinary Act of Extraordinary Love
Author: Jim Burns
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/homeword-mar-8-2010-11627199.html
Passage: Luke 10:36-37
Points:
- The beaten traveler was in desperate need, yet religious passersby failed to assist him.
- The priest maintained an outward appearance of piety but lived with inward hypocrisy.
- The Levite meant well but allowed personal busyness and self-centeredness to crowd out compassion.
- The Samaritan crossed cultural and social divides, sacrificing his time and money to help a stranger.
- Christ calls ordinary believers to demonstrate extraordinary love through tangible mercy.

### Lessons from the Good Samaritan
Author: Ken Jones
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/lessons-from-the-good-samaritan
Passage: Luke 10:25-37
Points:
- A legal expert tested Jesus under the assumption that eternal life could be earned through Law-keeping.
- Jesus highlighted wholehearted love for God and neighbor to show man's need for a Savior.
- Love for God is inseparable from love for others; genuine faith always expresses itself horizontally.
- The Samaritan's rescue of the helpless traveler mirrors Christ's saving grace toward fallen sinners.
- The gospel dismantles cultural prejudice and calls believers to view every image bearer as a neighbor.

### The Parable of the Good Samaritan
Author: Tabletalk Magazine
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://www.ligonier.org/learn/devotionals/parable-good-samaritan
Passage: Luke 10:25-37
Points:
- Jesus' choice of a Samaritan hero shocked listeners because Jews and Samaritans harbored deep mutual hostility.
- Pointing to the great commandments exposed the lawyer's inability to achieve eternal life by his own merit.
- Unlike the priest and Levite who avoided inconvenience, the Samaritan offered immediate and sacrificial help.
- God commands that neighborly love not be restricted by ethnicity, social status, or bloodlines.
- While Christians share spiritual brotherhood only in Christ, all human beings belong to our universal neighborhood.

### 5 Ways Christians Can Apply the Parable of the Good Samaritan Today
Author: Meg Bucher
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/spiritual-life/bible-parable-of-the-good-samaritan.html
Passage: Luke 10:36-37
Points:
- Believers must deliberately slow down in a fast-paced world to notice hurting people in their daily path.
- Regular prayer prepares our hearts to view strangers with compassion rather than fear or indifference.
- When an opportunity to help arises, Christians should respond promptly instead of hesitating or making excuses.
- Remembering God's past mercy in our own struggles fosters humility and empathy toward others.
- Biblical neighborly love requires generous stewardship, offering our own time and resources to meet practical needs.
